sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atha nārāyaṇenendraś cakāra saha saṃvidam avatartuṃ mahīṃ svargād aṃśataḥ sahitaḥ suraiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Indra, together with Nārāyaṇa, made an agreement to descend to earth from heaven, accompanied by the gods, each taking a partial incarnation.

sanskrit: ādiśya ca svayaṃ śakraḥ sarvān eva divaukasaḥ nirjagāma punas tasmāt kṣayān nārāyaṇasya ha
english: And Śakra himself, having instructed all the heaven-dwellers, departed once again from the abode of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: te 'marārivināśāya sarvalokahitāya ca avateruḥ krameṇemāṃ mahīṃ svargād divaukasaḥ
english: For the destruction of the enemies of the immortals and for the welfare of all the worlds, those heaven-dwellers descended in succession from heaven to this earth.

sanskrit: tato brahmarṣivaṃśeṣu pārthivarṣikuleṣu ca jajñire rājaśārdūla yathākāmaṃ divaukasaḥ
english: Then, O tiger among kings, those heaven-dwellers were born at will in the lineages of brahmarshis and in the royal families of earthly sages.

sanskrit: dānavān rākṣasāṃś caiva gandharvān pannagāṃs tathā puruṣādāni cānyāni jaghnuḥ sattvāny anekaśaḥ
english: They slew danavas and rakshasas, gandharvas and nagas, and many other man-eating beings in great numbers.

sanskrit: dānavā rākṣasāś caiva gandharvāḥ pannagās tathā na tān balasthān bālye 'pi jaghnur bharatasattama
english: But the danavas, rakshasas, gandharvas, and nagas — those mighty ones — could not slay them even in childhood, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca devadānavasaṃghānāṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ tathā mānavānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ tathā vai yakṣarakṣasām
english: Janamejaya said: Of the assemblies of gods and danavas, of gandharvas and apsaras, of all humans, and also of yakshas and rakshasas —

sanskrit: śrotum icchāmi tattvena saṃbhavaṃ kṛtsnam āditaḥ prāṇināṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ sarvaśaḥ sarvavid dhyasi
english: I wish to hear truly, from the very beginning, the complete origin of all these, and of all living beings in their entirety — for you know all things.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi namaskṛtvā svayaṃbhuve surādīnām ahaṃ samyag lokānāṃ prabhavāpyayam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Well then, I shall tell you — having bowed to the Self-born — the origin and dissolution of the worlds, beginning with the gods, completely and correctly.

sanskrit: brahmaṇo mānasāḥ putrā viditāḥ ṣaṇ maharṣayaḥ marīcir atryaṅgirasau pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ
english: The six great sages known as the mind-born sons of Brahmā are: Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu.

sanskrit: marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ putraḥ kaśyapāt tu imāḥ prajāḥ prajajñire mahābhāgā dakṣakanyās trayodaśa
english: Kaśyapa is the son of Marīci, and from Kaśyapa were born these offspring. The thirteen highly blessed daughters of Dakṣa gave birth to these creatures.

sanskrit: aditir ditir danuḥ kālā anāyuḥ siṃhikā muniḥ krodhā prāvā ariṣṭā ca vinatā kapilā tathā
english: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kala, Anayus, Siṃhikā, Muni, Krodha, Prava, Ariṣṭa, Vinatā, and Kapila —

sanskrit: kadrūś ca manujavyāghra dakṣakanyaiva bhārata etāsāṃ vīryasaṃpannaṃ putrapautram anantakam
english: — and Kadrū, O tiger among men, these daughters of Dakṣa, O Bharata: the offspring — sons and grandsons — of these ladies, endowed with might, is without end.

sanskrit: adityāṃ dvādaśādityāḥ saṃbhūtā bhuvaneśvarāḥ ye rājan nāmatas tāṃs te kīrtayiṣyāmi bhārata
english: From Aditi were born the twelve Ādityas, lords of the worlds. I shall name them for you, O king, O Bharata.

sanskrit: dhātā mitro 'ryamā śakro varuṇaś cāṃśa eva ca bhago vivasvān pūṣā ca savitā daśamas tathā
english: Dhata, Mitra, Aryamā, Śakra, Varuṇa, and Amsha; Bhaga, Vivasvat, Pusha, and Savitā the tenth —

sanskrit: ekādaśas tathā tvaṣṭā viṣṇur dvādaśa ucyate jaghanyajaḥ sa sarveṣām ādityānāṃ guṇādhikaḥ
english: — Tvaṣṭā the eleventh, and Viṣṇu is declared the twelfth. He, the last-born of all the Ādityas, surpasses them all in virtues.

sanskrit: eka eva diteḥ putro hiraṇyakaśipuḥ smṛtaḥ nāmnā khyātās tu tasyeme putrāḥ pañca mahātmanaḥ
english: Diti had but one son, remembered as Hiraṇyakaśipu. These five sons of that great-souled one were known by the following names:

sanskrit: prahrādaḥ pūrvajas teṣāṃ saṃhrādas tadanantaram anuhrādas tṛtīyo 'bhūt tasmāc ca śibibāṣkalau
english: Prahlāda was the eldest among them, then Saṃhrāda next; Anuhlada was the third, and after him came Śibi and Bāṣkala.

sanskrit: prahrādasya trayaḥ putrāḥ khyātāḥ sarvatra bhārata virocanaś ca kumbhaś ca nikumbhaś ceti viśrutāḥ
english: Prahlāda had three sons known everywhere, O Bharata: Virocana, Kumbha, and Nikumbha, all renowned.

sanskrit: virocanasya putro 'bhūd balir ekaḥ pratāpavān baleś ca prathitaḥ putro bāṇo nāma mahāsuraḥ
english: Virocana had one son, the mighty Bali; and Bali's famous son was the great asura named Bana.

sanskrit: catvāriṃśad danoḥ putrāḥ khyātāḥ sarvatra bhārata teṣāṃ prathamajo rājā vipracittir mahāyaśāḥ
english: Danu had forty sons known everywhere, O Bharata; the eldest among them was the king Vipracitti, of great renown.

sanskrit: śambaro namuciś caiva pulomā ceti viśrutaḥ asilomā ca keśī ca durjayaś caiva dānavaḥ
english: Śambara, Namuci, the renowned Pulomā; Asiloma, Keśī, and the danava Durjaya —

sanskrit: ayaḥśirā aśvaśirā ayaḥśaṅkuś ca vīryavān tathā gaganamūrdhā ca vegavān ketumāṃś ca yaḥ
english: — Ayaḥśirā, Ashvashira, and the mighty Ayahshanku; Gaganamurdha, the swift Ketuman —

sanskrit: svarbhānur aśvo 'śvapatir vṛṣaparvājakas tathā aśvagrīvaś ca sūkṣmaś ca tuhuṇḍaś ca mahāsuraḥ
english: — Svarbhānu, Aśva, Aśvapati, Vṛṣaparvā and Ajaka; Ashvagrīva, Sukshma, and the great asura Tuhunda —

sanskrit: isṛpā ekacakraś ca virūpākṣo harāharau nicandraś ca nikumbhaś ca kupathaḥ kāpathas tathā
english: — Isripa, Ekacakra, Virūpākṣa, Hara and Ahara; Nicandra, Nikumbha, Kupatha, and Kapatha —

sanskrit: śarabhaḥ śalabhaś caiva sūryācandramasau tathā iti khyātā danor vaṃśe dānavāḥ parikīrtitāḥ anyau tu khalu devānāṃ sūryācandramasau smṛtau
english: — Śarabha, Śalabha, and also the pair Sūrya and Candramā: thus are the danavas of Danu's lineage enumerated. But those two — Sūrya and Candramā — are indeed remembered as belonging to the gods.

sanskrit: ime ca vaṃśe prathitāḥ sattvavanto mahābalāḥ danuputrā mahārāja daśa dānavapuṅgavāḥ
english: And these ten bull-like danavas, famous in their lineage, full of vitality and mighty in strength, are the sons of Danu, O great king.

sanskrit: ekākṣo mṛtapā vīraḥ pralambanarakāv api vātāpiḥ śatrutapanaḥ śaṭhaś caiva mahāsuraḥ
english: Ekaksha, the heroic Mritapa, Pralamba and Naraka; Vātāpi, Shatrutapana, and the great asura Shatha —

sanskrit: gaviṣṭhaś ca danāyuś ca dīrghajihvaś ca dānavaḥ asaṃkhyeyāḥ smṛtās teṣāṃ putrāḥ pautrāś ca bhārata
english: — Gaviṣṭha, Danayu, and the danava Dirghajihva. Their sons and grandsons are remembered as innumerable, O Bharata.

sanskrit: siṃhikā suṣuve putraṃ rāhuṃ candrārkamardanam sucandraṃ candrahantāraṃ tathā candravimardanam
english: Siṃhikā bore the son Rāhu, the afflicting force of moon and sun; also Suchandra, the moon-slayer, and Chandravimardana.

sanskrit: krūrasvabhāvaṃ krūrāyāḥ putrapautram anantakam gaṇaḥ krodhavaśo nāma krūrakarmārimardanaḥ
english: The offspring — sons and grandsons — of this cruel-natured woman are without end; the host called Krodhavaśa, of cruel deeds and destroyer of enemies.

sanskrit: anāyuṣaḥ punaḥ putrāś catvāro 'surapuṃgavāḥ vikṣaro balavīrau ca vṛtraś caiva mahāsuraḥ
english: Anayus had four bull-like asura sons: Vikshara, Bala, Vīra, and the great asura Vṛtra.

sanskrit: kālāyāḥ prathitāḥ putrāḥ kālakalpāḥ prahāriṇaḥ bhuvi khyātā mahāvīryā dānaveṣu paraṃtapāḥ
english: The renowned sons of Kala, resembling Death itself in their striking power, are known on earth as mighty in valor among the danavas, afflicting their foes.

sanskrit: vināśanaś ca krodhaś ca hantā krodhasya cāparaḥ krodhaśatrus tathaivānyaḥ kāleyā iti viśrutāḥ
english: Vinashana, Krodha, Hanta the other son of Krodha, and likewise Krodhashatru — these are renowned as the Kāleyas.

sanskrit: asurāṇām upādhyāyaḥ śukras tv ṛṣisuto 'bhavat khyātāś cośanasaḥ putrāś catvāro 'surayājakāḥ
english: Śukra, son of the sage Bhṛgu, became the preceptor of the asuras. The four famous sons of Uśanas were officiant priests for the asuras.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭāvaras tathātriś ca dvāv anyau mantrakarmiṇau tejasā sūryasaṃkāśā brahmalokaprabhāvanāḥ
english: Tvashtavara, Atri, and two others — performers of sacred rites — blazing in splendor equal to the sun, and powerful enough to illuminate Brahmā's world.

sanskrit: ity eṣa vaṃśaprabhavaḥ kathitas te tarasvinām asurāṇāṃ surāṇāṃ ca purāṇe saṃśruto mayā
english: Thus has this origin of lineages been told to you — of the vigorous asuras and the gods — as I have heard it in the Purāṇa.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ yad apatyaṃ tu na śakyaṃ tad aśeṣataḥ prasaṃkhyātuṃ mahīpāla guṇabhūtam anantakam
english: The offspring of these beings — qualities included — cannot be fully enumerated in its entirety, O lord of the earth; it is without end.

sanskrit: tārkṣyaś cāriṣṭanemiś ca tathaiva garuḍāruṇau āruṇir vāruṇiś caiva vainateyā iti smṛtāḥ
english: Tārkṣya, Ariṣṭanemi, and likewise Garuḍa and Aruṇa; Aruni and Varuni — these are remembered as the sons of Vinatā.

sanskrit: śeṣo 'nanto vāsukiś ca takṣakaś ca bhujaṃgamaḥ kūrmaś ca kulikaś caiva kādraveyā mahābalāḥ
english: Śeṣa, Ananta, Vāsuki, the serpent Takṣaka, Kurma, and Kulika — these mighty sons of Kadrū are the Kadruveyas.

sanskrit: bhīmasenograsenau ca suparṇo varuṇas tathā gopatir dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca sūryavarcāś ca saptamaḥ
english: Bhīmasena, Ugrasena, Suparṇa, and Varuṇa; Gopati, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Suryavarchas the seventh —

sanskrit: patravān arkaparṇaś ca prayutaś caiva viśrutaḥ bhīmaś citrarathaś caiva vikhyātaḥ sarvavid vaśī
english: — Puravin, Arkaparna, and the renowned Prayuta; the celebrated Bhīma and Chitraratha, known as all-knowing and self-controlled —

sanskrit: tathā śāliśirā rājan pradyumnaś ca caturdaśaḥ kaliḥ pañcadaśaś caiva nāradaś caiva ṣoḍaśaḥ ity ete devagandharvā mauneyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ
english: — and Shalishira, O king, Pradyumna the fourteenth, Kali the fifteenth, and Nārada the sixteenth — thus are these divine gandharvas, the Mauneyas, enumerated.

sanskrit: atas tu bhūtāny anyāni kīrtayiṣyāmi bhārata anavadyām anuvaśām anūnām aruṇāṃ priyām anūpāṃ subhagāṃ bhāsīm iti prāvā vyajāyata
english: Now I shall name other beings, O Bharata. Prava gave birth to: the blameless Anuvasham, Anunam, Aruṇa, Priya, Anūpa, Subhaga, and Bhasi.

sanskrit: siddhaḥ pūrṇaś ca barhī ca pūrṇāśaś ca mahāyaśāḥ brahmacārī ratiguṇaḥ suparṇaś caiva saptamaḥ
english: Siddha, Purna, Barhi, the greatly renowned Purnasha, Brahmachari, Ratiguṇa, and Suparṇa the seventh —

sanskrit: viśvāvasuś ca bhānuś ca sucandro daśamas tathā ity ete devagandharvāḥ prāveyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ
english: — Viśvāvasu, Bhānu, and Suchandra the tenth: thus are these divine gandharvas, the sons of Prava, enumerated.

sanskrit: imaṃ tv apsarasāṃ vaṃśaṃ viditaṃ puṇyalakṣaṇam prāvāsūta mahābhāgā devī devarṣitaḥ purā
english: This lineage of the apsaras, known for its auspicious qualities — the highly blessed goddess Prava bore it long ago, as received from the divine sages.

sanskrit: alambusā miśrakeṣī vidyutparṇā tulānaghā aruṇā rakṣitā caiva rambhā tadvan manoramā
english: Alambusa, Miśrakeśī, Vidyutparna, Tulanagha, Aruṇa, Rakshita, Rambha, and likewise Manorama —

sanskrit: asitā ca subāhuś ca suvratā subhujā tathā supriyā cātibāhuś ca vikhyātau ca hahāhuhū tumburuś ceti catvāraḥ smṛtā gandharvasattamāḥ
english: — Asita, Subāhu, Suvrata, Subhuja, Supriya, and Atibahu; and the renowned Haha, Hūhū, and Tumburu are remembered as the four foremost gandharvas.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ brāhmaṇā gāvo gandharvāpsarasas tathā apatyaṃ kapilāyās tu purāṇe parikīrtitam
english: Amrita, brahmanas, cows, gandharvas, and apsaras — these are celebrated in the Purāṇa as the offspring of Kapila.

sanskrit: iti te sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃbhavaḥ kathito mayā yathāvat parisaṃkhyāto gandharvāpsarasāṃ tathā
english: Thus has the origin of all beings been told to you by me, counted out correctly, and likewise that of the gandharvas and apsaras.

sanskrit: bhujagānāṃ suparṇānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ marutāṃ tathā gavāṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca śrīmatāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām
english: Of serpents and of suparnas, of the Rudras and the Maruts, of cows and of brahmanas — of the glorious ones of meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: āyuṣyaś caiva puṇyaś ca dhanyaḥ śrutisukhāvahaḥ śrotavyaś caiva satataṃ śrāvyaś caivānasūyatā
english: This account is life-prolonging, meritorious, and enriching; it is pleasant to hear, should always be listened to, and should be narrated with a heart free from envy.

sanskrit: imaṃ tu vaṃśaṃ niyamena yaḥ paṭhen; mahātmanāṃ brāhmaṇadevasaṃnidhau apatyalābhaṃ labhate sa puṣkalaṃ; śriyaṃ yaśaḥ pretya ca śobhanāṃ gatim
english: Whoever recites this lineage of great souls with discipline in the presence of brahmanas and gods gains abundant progeny, prosperity, and renown, and after death an excellent destination.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca brahmaṇo mānasāḥ putrā viditāḥ ṣaṇ maharṣayaḥ ekādaśa sutāḥ sthāṇoḥ khyātāḥ paramamānasāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The six great sages, known as the mind-born sons of Brahmā, are well known. The eleven supremely mind-born sons of Sthāṇu (Śiva) are also renowned.

sanskrit: mṛgavyādhaś ca śarvaś ca nirṛtiś ca mahāyaśāḥ ajaikapād ahirbudhnyaḥ pinākī ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: Mrigavyadha, Śarva, the greatly renowned Nirṛti; Ajaikapat, Ahirbudhnya, and Pinaki the scorcher of foes —

sanskrit: dahano 'theśvaraś caiva kapālī ca mahādyutiḥ sthāṇur bhavaś ca bhagavān rudrā ekādaśa smṛtāḥ
english: — Dahana, Ishvara, Kapali of great splendor, Sthāṇu, and the lord Bhava: these are remembered as the eleven Rudras.

sanskrit: marīcir aṅgirā atriḥ pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ ṣaḍ ete brahmaṇaḥ putrā vīryavanto maharṣayaḥ
english: Marīci, Aṅgiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu — these six are the mighty great-sage sons of Brahmā.

sanskrit: trayas tv aṅgirasaḥ putrā loke sarvatra viśrutāḥ bṛhaspatir utathyaś ca saṃvartaś ca dhṛtavratāḥ
english: Aṅgiras had three sons renowned everywhere in the world: Bṛhaspati, Utathya, and Saṃvarta — all firm in their vows.

sanskrit: atres tu bahavaḥ putrāḥ śrūyante manujādhipa sarve vedavidaḥ siddhāḥ śāntātmāno maharṣayaḥ
english: Atri had many sons, O lord of men — all knowers of the Vedas, perfected, tranquil-souled great sages, as is told.

sanskrit: rākṣasās tu pulastyasya vānarāś ca kiṃnarās tathā pulahasya mṛgāḥ siṃhā vyāghrāḥ kiṃpuruṣās tathā
english: Rākṣasas came from Pulastya, as did vanaras and kinnaras. From Pulaha came deer, lions, tigers, and kimpurushas.

sanskrit: kratoḥ kratusamāḥ putrāḥ pataṃgasahacāriṇaḥ viśrutās triṣu lokeṣu satyavrataparāyaṇāḥ
english: Kratu's sons are equal to Kratu himself in power, companions of birds in flight, renowned throughout the three worlds, and wholly devoted to the vow of truth.

sanskrit: dakṣas tv ajāyatāṅguṣṭhād dakṣiṇād bhagavān ṛṣiḥ brahmaṇaḥ pṛthivīpāla putraḥ putravatāṃ varaḥ
english: Dakṣa, the blessed sage, was born from the right thumb of Brahmā, O protector of the earth — the best of those who have sons.

sanskrit: vāmād ajāyatāṅguṣṭhād bhāryā tasya mahātmanaḥ tasyāṃ pañcāśataṃ kanyāḥ sa evājanayan muniḥ
english: From Brahmā's left thumb was born the wife of that great-souled one; and the sage himself fathered fifty daughters upon her.

sanskrit: tāḥ sarvās tv anavadyāṅgyaḥ kanyāḥ kamalalocanāḥ putrikāḥ sthāpayām āsa naṣṭaputraḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: All those daughters, faultless-limbed and lotus-eyed, the Prajāpati appointed as putrikas (daughters serving as sons), since he had no sons.

sanskrit: dadau sa daśa dharmāya saptaviṃśatim indave divyena vidhinā rājan kaśyapāya trayodaśa
english: He gave ten to Dharma, twenty-seven to Soma (the moon), by divine rule, O king, and thirteen to Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: nāmato dharmapatnyas tāḥ kīrtyamānā nibodha me kīrtir lakṣmīr dhṛtir medhā puṣṭiḥ śraddhā kriyā tathā
english: Learn from me the names of those wives of Dharma as I recite them: Kirti, Lakṣmī, Dhrti, Medha, Pushti, Śraddhā, and Kriya —

sanskrit: buddhir lajjā matiś caiva patnyo dharmasya tā daśa dvārāṇy etāni dharmasya vihitāni svayaṃbhuvā
english: — Buddhi, Lajja, and Mati: these are the ten wives of Dharma. These are the gateways of Dharma appointed by the Self-born.

sanskrit: saptaviṃśati somasya patnyo loke pariśrutāḥ kālasya nayane yuktāḥ somapatnyaḥ śubhavratāḥ sarvā nakṣatrayoginyo lokayātrāvidhau sthitāḥ
english: The twenty-seven wives of Soma are celebrated in the world; engaged in guiding time, wives of the moon, of pure vows, all connected to the nakshatras, established in the order of the world's journey.

sanskrit: pitāmaho munir devas tasya putraḥ prajāpatiḥ tasyāṣṭau vasavaḥ putrās teṣāṃ vakṣyāmi vistaram
english: The grandfather Muni is a god; his son is the Prajāpati (Dharma). That one had eight Vasus as sons — I shall speak of them in detail.

sanskrit: dharo dhruvaś ca somaś ca ahaś caivānilo 'nalaḥ pratyūṣaś ca prabhāsaś ca vasavo 'ṣṭāv iti smṛtāḥ
english: Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Aha, Anila, Anala, Pratyusha, and Prabhāsa — these are remembered as the eight Vasus.

sanskrit: dhūmrāyāś ca dharaḥ putro brahmavidyo dhruvas tathā candramās tu manasvinyāḥ śvasāyāḥ śvasanas tathā
english: Dhara is the son of Dhūmra, and similarly Dhruva is a knower of Brahmā. Soma is the son of Manasvinī; from Shvasa came Shvasana (Anila, the wind).

sanskrit: ratāyāś cāpy ahaḥ putraḥ śāṇḍilyāś ca hutāśanaḥ pratyūṣaś ca prabhāsaś ca prabhātāyāḥ sutau smṛtau
english: Aha is the son of Rata; Hutāśana (fire) is the son of Śāṇḍilya. Pratyusha and Prabhāsa are remembered as the two sons of Prabhata.

sanskrit: dharasya putro draviṇo hutahavyavahas tathā dhruvasya putro bhagavān kālo lokaprakālanaḥ
english: The sons of Dhara are Dravina and Hutahavyavaha (carrier of oblations). The son of Dhruva is the blessed Kala, who brings about the dissolution of the worlds.

sanskrit: somasya tu suto varcā varcasvī yena jāyate manoharāyāḥ śiśiraḥ prāṇo 'tha ramaṇas tathā
english: Soma's son is Varcha, by whom the radiant are born. From Manohara were born Shishira, Prāṇa, and Ramana.

sanskrit: ahnaḥ sutaḥ smṛto jyotiḥ śramaḥ śāntas tathā muniḥ agneḥ putraḥ kumāras tu śrīmāñ śaravaṇālayaḥ
english: The sons of Aha are remembered as Jyoti, Shrama, Shanta, and Muni. The son of Agni (Anala) is the glorious Kumāra, who dwells in the shara-grass forest.

sanskrit: tasya śākho viśākhaś ca naigameśaś ca pṛṣṭhajaḥ kṛttikābhyupapatteś ca kārttikeya iti smṛtaḥ
english: His sons are Shakha, Viśākha, and Naigameṣa born from his back. Because the Kṛttikās adopted him, he is remembered as Kārttikeya.

sanskrit: anilasya śivā bhāryā tasyāḥ putraḥ purojavaḥ avijñātagatiś caiva dvau putrāv anilasya tu
english: Śiva is the wife of Anila (the wind god); her son is Purojava. Avijnatagati is the other — these are the two sons of Anila.

sanskrit: pratyūṣasya viduḥ putram ṛṣiṃ nāmnātha devalam dvau putrau devalasyāpi kṣamāvantau manīṣiṇau
english: Pratyusha's son is known as the sage named Devala. Devala also had two sons — patient and wise.

sanskrit: bṛhaspates tu bhaginī varastrī brahmacāriṇī yogasiddhā jagat sarvam asaktaṃ vicaraty uta prabhāsasya tu bhāryā sā vasūnām aṣṭamasya ha
english: Bṛhaspati's sister, a noble woman, a celibate ascetic, accomplished in yoga, roams the entire world unattached — she is the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth of the Vasus.
